subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Learning a new language can be __all challenging and rewarding.__
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. both challenging and rewarding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined phrase "all challenging and rewarding" is grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended meaning properly.
 
• The correct substitution is **"both challenging and rewarding," **which clearly expresses that learning a new language is both of these qualities simultaneously.
 
• Using **"both"** emphasizes that the action or experience is equally challenging and rewarding.

Correct sentence: *Learning a new language can be **both challenging and rewarding**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common usage of "both":**

 
 
• "Both" is used to link two qualities or elements that coexist or are equally applicable.
 
 
• Example: She is both intelligent and kind.
 
• Usage: It emphasizes dual characteristics or actions.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Incorrect alternatives:**
 
 
• "Whether both challenging and rewarding" is awkward and does not fit the sentence structure.
 
• "All both challenging or rewarding" is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
 
• "Neither challenging and rewarding" changes the meaning of the sentence entirely.
